By CitiFMonline
Business & Finance
WED, 04 JAN 2017 2
Information gathered by **Citi Business News** indicates that Dr. Kofi Kodua Sarpong will be taking over from Mr. Alex Mould as the Chief Executive Officer(CEO) of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation(GNPC).
Mr. K.K Sarpong who was the former CEO of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) was appointed as the Executive Chairman of Asante Kotoko FC in 2010, but resigned in 2013.
He was until July 31, 2012 the Executive Chairman of Finatec Limited a consortium of Chartered Accountants, Lawyers and Investment Experts.
He had previously worked as the Deputy Managing Director and subsequently as the Managing Director of Tema Oil Refinery Limited from September 2003 to August 2009.
Dr. Sarpong garnered his International working experience with International Cocoa Organization as the Head of Administration and Financial Services Division from January 1999 to 2003.
At the Ghana Cocoa Board, Dr. Sarpong worked as Deputy Chief Executive (Finance and Administration) from 1994 to December 1998.
He worked with Produce Buying Company Limited as the Deputy Managing Director (Finance and Administration) from July 1990 to August 1994.
At Ghana Food Distribution Corporation, Dr. Sarpong worked in various capacities as Deputy Chief Accountant, Accountant and General Manager (Finance and Administration).

Dr. Sarpong has also served in Non-Executive and Advisory Positions in different organizations including serving on the boards of reputable Ghanaian banks including Ghana Commercial Bank and Merchant Bank from 1996 to 2010.
Dr. K.K. Sarpong is a Chartered Accountant and also holds a PhD in Industrial and Business Studies from the University of Warwick, M.Acc in International Accounting and Finance from the University of Glasgow.
He also holds an MBA in Accounting and B.Sc (Administration) Accounting Option from University of Ghana Legon.
At Kotoko, Dr. Sarpong enabled the club to rediscover their championship feat, winning the league title on a back to back basis.
He is currently the chairman of the Board of Directors of Royal Bank.

**Bashir Bayo Ojulari** is a Nigerian engineer and expert in petroleum, process and production engineering currently serving as Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd). In January 2024, Ojulari joined Renaissance African Energy Company as executive vice-president and chief operating officer and led a consortium of local energy companies in a $2.4 billion Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria (SPDC) acquisition deal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:2-1) He was managing director of Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company from 2015 to 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-4) President Bola Tinubu appointed him as the Group Chief Executive Officer of the NNPC Ltd on 2 April 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-6)
Ojulari graduated with a degree in Mechanical Engineering from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1989.

Ojulari is a Fellow of Nigerian Society of Engineers.His career in energy is focused on exploration, field development, production management, strategic planning and investment evaluation. He began his career in 1989 as a field and process engineer at Elf Petroleum Nigeria before moving to Shell in 1991 as an associate production technologist. At Shell, Ojulari worked in Europe and the Middle East in different managerial capacities in Petroleum Engineering, Process Engineering, Production Engineering and in health and safety roles.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-7) From June 1994 to October 1995, Ojulari served on the Shell integrated studies team at its headquarters in the Netherland. In late 1990, Ojulari served in different leadership positions in Nigeria engineering professional organisations including as chairman and member of board of trustees of Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE Nigeria Council) from 1998 to 1999.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-9)
In 1997, he became the head of planning, economics and budgeting of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) and served in this position until 1999 when he was transferred to Oman SPDC where he was head, production technologists and asset leader. In 2003, Ojulari returned to Shell headquarters as a regional planner for sub-Saharan Africa and later served in different capacities at SPDC including as manager corporate planning and strategy, and asset development (onshore and shallow water).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)
In 2010, Ojulari was appointed as a director at SPDC leading petroleum engineering of 100 oil and gas fields and 15 major projects with well budget of $700 million.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)

Ojulari was appointed Managing Director Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company and as general manager, Deepwater in November 2015. Within this period, he served as a member of the board of directors of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) responsible for Onshore and Offshore Petroleum Engineering, Technical Integration of Development, Well and Project Engineering.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-12) During his term he developed Nigeria’s first deepwater project - Bonga field and increased production to 320,000 barrels per day with cost-saving plan that reduced operational expenses by 30 per cent. He retired from his positions in Shell in July 2021.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-14)
In 2021, he founded BAT Advisory & Energy, a company specialising in upstream and midstream advisory serving as the chairman of its board. In January 2024, Ojulari joined Renaissance African Energy Company as executive vice-president and chief operating officer. In this position, he led a consortium of indigenous energy firms – ND Western, Aradel Energy, First Exploration & Production, Waltersmith, and Petrolin in a $2.4 billion Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria acquisition deal.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-15)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:2-1)

On 2 April 2025, Nigerian President Bola Tinubu appointed Ojulari as group chief executive officer (GCEO) of Nigeria state oil company, NNPC Limited.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-16) Ojulari initiated several reforms in the NNPC Limited operations including terminating crude oil swaps to fund inactive national oil refineries repairs to block revenue leakages and halted the direct involvement of the NNPC Limited in the Turnaround Maintenance (TAM) of same refineries which had costed the country over ₦13 trillion in two decades.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-17) He proposed a new model - Technical Equity Partnership which would give international operators majority controlling stake in the refineries reducing NNPC Limited’s equity stake down to between 10% and 40% for efficient running of the refineries.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-18)
In 2025, NNPC Limited recorded a “historic” profit after tax of ₦7.2 trillion for the 2025 financial year up 33% in profits year-on-year earnings[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-19) driven by Ojulari’s 25% cut in administrative running cost of NNPC Limited operations and debt recovery from outstanding balance on crude oil transactions owed to company by its long-standing customers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-20) Same period, joint-venture contract renegotiations freed up $3.4 billion in structural savings for the state oil company and Nigeria exceeded its Opec quota as crude oil output averaged 1.7 million barrels per day from average 1.55 mbpd prior to Ojulari’s administration.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-22)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
| Bashir Bayo Ojulari |  
| --- |  
|  |  
|  |  
| Group Chief Executive Officer of the NNPC Limited |  
| **Incumbent** |  
| **Assumed office** 2 April 2025 |  
| President | Bola Tinubu |  
| Preceded by | Mele Kyari |  
| Executive Vice-President and Chief Operating Officer, Renaissance African Energy Company |  
| **In office** January 2024–March 2025 |  
| Managing Director, Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company |  
| **In office** 2015–2021 |  
| Personal details |  
| Born | June 3, 1965 (age 61) Ilorin |  
| Occupation | Engineer |  
|  |
**Bashir Bayo Ojulari** is a Nigerian engineer and expert in petroleum, process and production engineering currently serving as Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd). In January 2024, Ojulari joined Renaissance African Energy Company as executive vice-president and chief operating officer and led a consortium of local energy companies in a $2.4 billion Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria (SPDC) acquisition deal.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:2-1) He was managing director of Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company from 2015 to 2021.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:0-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-4) President Bola Tinubu appointed him as the Group Chief Executive Officer of the NNPC Ltd on 2 April 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-6)
Ojulari graduated with a degree in Mechanical Engineering from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1989.
texts.1:
Ojulari is a Fellow of Nigerian Society of Engineers.His career in energy is focused on exploration, field development, production management, strategic planning and investment evaluation. He began his career in 1989 as a field and process engineer at Elf Petroleum Nigeria before moving to Shell in 1991 as an associate production technologist. At Shell, Ojulari worked in Europe and the Middle East in different managerial capacities in Petroleum Engineering, Process Engineering, Production Engineering and in health and safety roles.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-7) From June 1994 to October 1995, Ojulari served on the Shell integrated studies team at its headquarters in the Netherland. In late 1990, Ojulari served in different leadership positions in Nigeria engineering professional organisations including as chairman and member of board of trustees of Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE Nigeria Council) from 1998 to 1999.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-9)
In 1997, he became the head of planning, economics and budgeting of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) and served in this position until 1999 when he was transferred to Oman SPDC where he was head, production technologists and asset leader. In 2003, Ojulari returned to Shell headquarters as a regional planner for sub-Saharan Africa and later served in different capacities at SPDC including as manager corporate planning and strategy, and asset development (onshore and shallow water).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)
In 2010, Ojulari was appointed as a director at SPDC leading petroleum engineering of 100 oil and gas fields and 15 major projects with well budget of $700 million.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)
texts.2:
Ojulari was appointed Managing Director Shell Nigeria Exploration and Production Company and as general manager, Deepwater in November 2015. Within this period, he served as a member of the board of directors of Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC) responsible for Onshore and Offshore Petroleum Engineering, Technical Integration of Development, Well and Project Engineering.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-12) During his term he developed Nigeria’s first deepwater project - Bonga field and increased production to 320,000 barrels per day with cost-saving plan that reduced operational expenses by 30 per cent. He retired from his positions in Shell in July 2021.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-14)
In 2021, he founded BAT Advisory & Energy, a company specialising in upstream and midstream advisory serving as the chairman of its board. In January 2024, Ojulari joined Renaissance African Energy Company as executive vice-president and chief operating officer. In this position, he led a consortium of indigenous energy firms – ND Western, Aradel Energy, First Exploration & Production, Waltersmith, and Petrolin in a $2.4 billion Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria acquisition deal.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:1-11)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-15)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-:2-1)
texts.3:
On 2 April 2025, Nigerian President Bola Tinubu appointed Ojulari as group chief executive officer (GCEO) of Nigeria state oil company, NNPC Limited.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-16) Ojulari initiated several reforms in the NNPC Limited operations including terminating crude oil swaps to fund inactive national oil refineries repairs to block revenue leakages and halted the direct involvement of the NNPC Limited in the Turnaround Maintenance (TAM) of same refineries which had costed the country over ₦13 trillion in two decades.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-17) He proposed a new model - Technical Equity Partnership which would give international operators majority controlling stake in the refineries reducing NNPC Limited’s equity stake down to between 10% and 40% for efficient running of the refineries.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-18)
In 2025, NNPC Limited recorded a “historic” profit after tax of ₦7.2 trillion for the 2025 financial year up 33% in profits year-on-year earnings[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-19) driven by Ojulari’s 25% cut in administrative running cost of NNPC Limited operations and debt recovery from outstanding balance on crude oil transactions owed to company by its long-standing customers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-20) Same period, joint-venture contract renegotiations freed up $3.4 billion in structural savings for the state oil company and Nigeria exceeded its Opec quota as crude oil output averaged 1.7 million barrels per day from average 1.55 mbpd prior to Ojulari’s administration.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bashir_Ojulari#cite_note-22)

By CitiFMonline
General News
FRI, 27 JAN 2017
The Chief Executive Officer of the Bui Power Authority, Jabesh Amissah-Arthur, is proceeding on leave prior to his exit from office.
His leave begins today, Friday, January 27, 2017.
A memo sighted by **citifmonline.com**, signed by the outgoing CEO, and copied to staff of the company, noted that the Director for Programmes and Engineering Department, Mr. Anthony Boye Osafo-Kissi, will be responsible for the running of Bui Power until a substantive CEO is named by the President, Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.
“This is to inform all staff that I will be proceeding on my terminal leave from Friday 27th January 2017. While arranging to hand over to the President’s Representative as agreed with the Minister, the Director for Programmes and Engineering Department, Mr. Anthony Boye Osafo-Kissi, will be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Authority,” the memo added.
Jabesh Amissah-Arthur, brother of former Vice President, Kwesi Bekoe Amissah-Arthur, has been the CEO of company since the era of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government.
So far, all the Metropolitan Municipal and District Chief Executives, and heads of some government institutions have had their appointments terminated.
The head of COCOBOD and the National Petroleum Authority are among those that have been laid off.
–
By: Godwin A. Allotey/citifmonline.com/Ghana

Bui Dam
Mr. Jabesh Amissah-Arthur has quit his position as the Chief Executive Officer of Bui Power Authority, in charge of the country’s second largest hydro dam.
In a memo to the staff of the authority, he said he is taking his terminal leave from today, Friday, January 27, 2017 as he prepares to leave office.
The brother of former Vice President Paa Kwesi Amissah-Arthur was appointed by the previous government in 2009.
“While arranging to hand over to the president’s representative as agreed with the minister, the Director for Programs and Engineering Department, Mr. Anthony Boye Osafo-Kissi, would be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Authority,” Mr. Amissah-Arthur’s memo read.
He also urged his staff to extend to Mr. Osafo-Kissi, their usual cooperation.
The Bui Power Authority was established by the Act of Parliament, BPA Act 740, 2007 with a mandate to plan, execute and manage the Bui Hydroelectric Project.

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC), Abigail Elorm Mensah, has disclosed that the Centre, with support from National Security operatives, has retrieved three government vehicles from the residence of the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi.
Speaking on Citi FM’s _Eyewitness News_ on Wednesday, September 10, Mensah explained that the action formed part of a broader initiative to recover government loans and vehicles from defaulters.
“I have gone with National Security operatives to the house of the Chairman of the NPP in Ashanti Region, Chairman Wontumi. Three cars. In fact, the cars were five. We’ve retrieved three. I have collected all from his house. We are still chasing him for the two. He has to pay for them,” she revealed.

The MASLOC CEO noted that, under the Centre’s operational procedures, individuals who fail to meet repayment obligations or misuse government vehicles are required to either return the assets or settle their outstanding debts.
“What we do is that once I seize the cars, the agreement we have with you is that you would have to repay whatever has accrued and we release the cars to you,” she said.
Mensah added that several cases of asset misappropriation have already been reported to the police as part of efforts to safeguard public property.
“We’ve reported a lot of the issues to the police,” she confirmed.

By CitiFMonline
General News
FRI, 27 JAN 2017
The Chief Executive Officer of the Bui Power Authority, Jabesh Amissah-Arthur, is proceeding on leave prior to his exit from office.
His leave begins today, Friday, January 27, 2017.
A memo sighted by **citifmonline.com**, signed by the outgoing CEO, and copied to staff of the company, noted that the Director for Programmes and Engineering Department, Mr. Anthony Boye Osafo-Kissi, will be responsible for the running of Bui Power until a substantive CEO is named by the President, Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.
“This is to inform all staff that I will be proceeding on my terminal leave from Friday 27th January 2017. While arranging to hand over to the President’s Representative as agreed with the Minister, the Director for Programmes and Engineering Department, Mr. Anthony Boye Osafo-Kissi, will be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Authority,” the memo added.
Jabesh Amissah-Arthur, brother of former Vice President, Kwesi Bekoe Amissah-Arthur, has been the CEO of company since the era of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government.
So far, all the Metropolitan Municipal and District Chief Executives, and heads of some government institutions have had their appointments terminated.
The head of COCOBOD and the National Petroleum Authority are among those that have been laid off.
–

Bui Dam
Mr. Jabesh Amissah-Arthur has quit his position as the Chief Executive Officer of Bui Power Authority, in charge of the country’s second largest hydro dam.
In a memo to the staff of the authority, he said he is taking his terminal leave from today, Friday, January 27, 2017 as he prepares to leave office.
The brother of former Vice President Paa Kwesi Amissah-Arthur was appointed by the previous government in 2009.
“While arranging to hand over to the president’s representative as agreed with the minister, the Director for Programs and Engineering Department, Mr. Anthony Boye Osafo-Kissi, would be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Authority,” Mr. Amissah-Arthur’s memo read.
He also urged his staff to extend to Mr. Osafo-Kissi, their usual cooperation.
The Bui Power Authority was established by the Act of Parliament, BPA Act 740, 2007 with a mandate to plan, execute and manage the Bui Hydroelectric Project.

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC), Abigail Elorm Mensah has revealed that MASCLOC with assistance from National Security agents has retrieved three state vehicles from the residence of the Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, also known as Chairman Wontumi.
In an interview on Citi FM, Wednesday, September 10, 2025, the CEO explained that the action was part of a larger effort to recoup government loans and vehicles from defaulters.
“I have gone with National Security operatives to the house of the Chairman of the NPP in Ashanti Region, Chairman Wontumi. Three cars. In fact, the cars were five. We’ve retrieved three. I have collected all from his house. We are still chasing him for the two. He has to pay for them,” she noted.
According to MASLOC CEO, per the Center's operational regulations, anyone who abuse government cars or neglect their repayment duties must either surrender the assets or pay off their outstanding debts.
“What we do is that once I seize the cars, the agreement we have with you is that you would have to repay whatever has accrued and we release the cars to you,” she said.
Elorm Mensah noted that her outfit has reported to the police multiple cases of asset misappropriation, in an endeavor to protect public property.
“We’ve reported a lot of the issues to the police,” she confirmed.
Citing another example, Mensah recounted an incident involving a relative of former Vice President who took a government vehicle—a Nissan Urvan— and was reluctant to return it.
“I have a situation where a brother of former Vice President, Seidu Imoro picks a car and he is bold to tell us that ‘well he has used the car to work and he’s bought his own, so if we want we could come for it.’ So we’ve seized it,” she stated.

Jim Shaw has stepped down as CEO of Calgary-based Shaw Communications, advancing the date for his resignation from next year, the date the company first announced on Oct. 22.
CBC News
· Posted: Nov 18, 2010 12:41 PM EST | Last Updated: November 18, 2010
Listen to this article
Estimated 2 minutes
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.
Jim Shaw has stepped down as CEO of Calgary-based Shaw Communications, advancing the date for his resignation from next year, the date first announced on Oct. 22.
The company announced late Wednesday that Shaw has been succeeded by his brother, Brad.
Jim Shaw, shown at a shareholders meeting in 2008, has left earlier than originally announced as CEO of Shaw Communications.((Jeff McIntosh/Canadian Press))
"We are well underway in the integration of the Shaw Media assets," Jim Shaw was quoted as saying in a news release from the media and internet company, "and it became clear to Brad and I that it would be best for Brad to assume the role of CEO immediately so that he can move forward with the necessary decisions."
Jim Shaw, who is in his 50s, served as CEO of the company founded by his father, J.R. Shaw, for 12 years. He will continue as a vice-chair and a member of the board. Peter Bissonnette will continue as president and a member of the board.
Brad Shaw, 46, takes over leadership one month after the firm bought the television assets of Canwest Global Communications for $2 billion last month and as it creates a network to handle its planned wireless business.
"There has never been a more exciting time in our industry and I look forward, along with our very talented management team, to building upon the legacy that my father and brother have established as chief executive officers" Brad Shaw said in the release.

"There has never been a more exciting time in our industry and I look forward, along with our very talented management team, to building upon the legacy that my father and brother have established as chief executive officers" Brad Shaw said in the release.
